MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 P-H3 Image needs ComfyUI 0.44.0 or newer, the first version with these nodes. On an older ComfyUI the nodes show red: update ComfyUI first.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors19.5 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/h3

Create the h3 folder if it does not exist. This is the First and Last Frame version of MiniMax H3 (fl2va): if you did Episode 41 you may already have it.

 LoRA (in LoRA Loader Pixaroma)

Download p-h3-image_lora_bf16.safetensors1.82 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/h3

Create the h3 folder inside loras if it does not exist.

 Load CLIP

Download p-h3-image_text_encoder_int8_convrot.safetensors4.77 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load VAE

Download p-h3-image_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors2.93 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 Style Transfer LoRA (in LoRA Loader Pixaroma)

The Style Transfer LoRA by Alissonerdx: copies the look of your second picture. It was made for H3 video, and it works on P-H3 Image too. If you did Episode 41 you may already have it.

Download minimax_h3_style_transfer_v1.0_r64.safetensors592 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/h3

Made by Alissonerdx. Free to use, also for paid work; read the licence on the page.

Alissonerdx LoRAs and licence 

 License

P-H3 Image is built on MiniMax H3, so the MiniMax H3 Community License applies. Read it and check what it says for your country before you use the model.

READ LICENSE P-H3 Image model page 

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma: update to the latest version (these workflows need at least 1.4.183). A node shows red or missing? Update Pixaroma.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Latest Pixaroma version How to update Pixaroma 

 Something missing?

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Red or missing nodes A model file is missing Buttons missing after an update 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Give the model a photo and a second picture, and your photo comes out in the look of that picture: its colours, its shapes, its way of drawing. There is nothing to describe. The demo turns a photo of a woman in a cafe into a screen print, with the colours of the lighthouse print.

 Steps

  1. Load your photo in the first Load Image Mini Pixaroma.
  2. Load the picture with the style in the second one.
  3. Leave the prompt as it is.
  4. Click a size on Number Pick Pixaroma if you want a smaller or bigger result.
  5. Switch the seed to R to try a new one every Run, or leave it on F to repeat a result.
  6. Press Run. Drag across Image Compare Pixaroma to see before and after.

 Which style pictures work

  • Flat graphic styles work best. Our screen print worked on a portrait, a person and a house, on all 14 runs at the demo strength.
  • A cut paper style gave flat colours on 6 of 8 runs at strength 1, a softer change than the print.
  • A detailed comic panel mostly passed on its contrast and colours, and the photo stayed close to a photo.
  • Thick oil and watercolor barely changed a portrait: it stayed a photo with new colours. The oil did paint the house, on 2 of 2 runs.

 Good to know

  • Stay at 4 megapixels or below. At 8 megapixels the model gave back the lighthouse print on 2 of 3 seeds, so this workflow has no 8 button.
  • Your second picture came back unchanged? Try another seed. With the comic and the paper style, seed 1 did this every time at strength 1.
  • The strength of the Style Transfer LoRA matters. At 0.7, the demo, she keeps her face, her hair and the cafe. At 1 the colours follow the style picture harder, and her red hair went dark on 3 of 4 seeds.
  • Every seed is a different print. The colours, the background and the shapes all change, so try a few.
  • The LoRA does the work. Without it, the same idea gave back the second picture or left the photo alone on 24 of 24 runs.
  • The result has the shape of your photo. The demo goes in at 1024 x 1024 and comes out at 2048 x 2048.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video 

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"How to Use","icon":"to-do","color":"#2a9d8f"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 fl2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. The LoRA in the next node turns it into P-H3 Image, a picture model. If you did Episode 41 you may already have this file.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (P-H3 Image + Style Transfer) - Holds two LoRAs and both stay ON: the P-H3 Image LoRA makes H3 a picture model, the Style Transfer LoRA copies the look of your second picture. The style LoRA sits at 0.7: at 1 the colours follow the style picture harder.
  • Load CLIP (P-H3 Image text encoder) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the model understands. The type must be minimax.
  • Load VAE (P-H3 Image VAE) - Turns the finished render into the picture. It is made for P-H3 Image, a different file from the H3 video VAE.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. your photo) - The photo that changes style. The result takes the shape of this picture. Click it to upload your own, or pick one from the list.
  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (2. the style) - The picture whose look you want. Flat graphic styles work best (see How to Use). Click it to upload your own, or pick one from the list.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (3. leave it as it is) - The sentence the LoRA was trained on. It starts with style_transfer:, the word that wakes the LoRA up. Leave it as it is.
  • Number Pick Pixaroma (4. megapixels) - How big the result is. Click 1, 2 or 4 (the demo) megapixels. There is no 8 here: at 8 the model gave back the style picture on most seeds.
  • Seed Pixaroma (5. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) repeats the result, R (random) tries a new one every Run. Each seed gives a different print here. The demo uses seed 4.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (1 / 1 for pictures) - The noise schedule. P-H3 Image needs 1 and 1. Leave it as it is.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • Scale Image to Total Pixels (scales your picture) - Scales your picture to the size you clicked on Number Pick Pixaroma. The result comes out the same size and shape.
  • PH3 Image Conditioning (prompt + both pictures) - Joins the prompt and both pictures. image_1 is your photo, image_2 the style. With width and height on 0, the result takes the size and shape of your photo.
  • Basic Guider (no CFG) - Hands the model and the prompt to the sampler. P-H3 Image needs no CFG and no negative prompt.
  • KSampler Select (sampler) - The sampler. euler is the one in Pruna's own workflow. ComfyUI's template uses er_sde: the same speed, but it broke small words on a label in our tests.
  • Manual Sigmas (the 8 steps) - The 8 steps the model was trained on. More steps do not help, so leave these numbers as they are.
  • Random Noise - The starting noise, from the seed.
  • Sampler Custom Advanced (the render) - The render itself: 8 steps. The normal KSampler cannot take this hand-made step list, so this node does the job.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the result) - Saves each result as PNG into ComfyUI/output/P-H3 Image Style and shows it on the node.
  • Image Compare Pixaroma (before and after, drag across it) - Your photo and the result on top of each other. Drag across it to see the style change.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: a smaller picture is much faster.

SizeTime
1 megapixelabout 12 s
2 megapixelsabout 20 s
4 megapixels (the demo)27 to 39 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3, and 10 GB for the LoRA, the text encoder and the VAE), so it takes longer. After that they stay in memory, if your PC has enough of it. Two testers with 16 GB cards: with 64 GB of RAM the next Runs were close to the times above; with 32 GB the models loaded from disk again on every Run, and each Run took about 4 times as long.

 On a smaller card

Click 1 or 2 on Number Pick Pixaroma.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
